## Findings
- claim-1: For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\) has two Schur generating families indexed respectively by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) and \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\), each of size \(\binom{a+b}{a}\). [source-2@L1380-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: The paper formally conjectures that both such generating sets are minimal, and reports finite computer verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1489-L1502|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: The stronger unresolved statement is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\); the authors state that a proof had eluded them. [source-2@L1536-L1552|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: The source directory also records the related open question of finding a minimal generating set for \(I_w\) in type \(A_{n-1}\). [source-6@L88-L102|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-5: If \(Q\) is generated by marked elements \(g_1,\ldots,g_N\), and for every \(\ell\) there is a prime \(p_\ell\) such that \(g_\ell\) has nonzero image in \(Q/(\sum_{k\ne\ell}\mathbb Zg_k+p_\ell Q)\), then \(\{g_\ell\}\) is inclusion-minimal.
- claim-6: Minimality does not imply the stronger torsion-free quotient conjecture: the standard basis minimally generates \((\mathbb Z/2)^N\), although this group is not \(\mathbb Z^N\).
## Strategy
Use the source-backed \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) Schur families as marked generators of
\[
Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v.
\]
A direct proof of the stronger authorial suspicion \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\) requires a complete integral presentation
\[
Q\cong\operatorname{coker}(R:\mathbb Z^s\to\mathbb Z^m).
\]
It is then equivalent to prove
\[
\operatorname{rank}R=m-N
\]
and that every nonzero Smith invariant factor of \(R\) is \(1\). Merely proving unimodularity of selected relation minors does not establish the required rank globally.

Conditional low-degree Pieri certificates establish this mechanism in restricted boundary cases, but not the required all-degree relation presentation.

## Gaps
No complete degreewise Schur-column and Pieri-row presentation of \(Q\) is source-grounded or proved here. In particular, missing are:

- completeness of all \(\Lambda_+J_v\) relations;
- the relation ranks in every degree;
- Smith-normal-form torsion control;
- proof that the proposed \(N\) generator images are independent in \(Q\).

Thus there is presently no direct proof of minimality or of the stronger freeness suspicion. Minimality alone would not imply freeness, as noted by the \(N\ge1\) example \((\mathbb Z/2)^N\).

## Next
Obtain a complete integral graded presentation of \(Q\), then apply the rank-plus-Smith criterion degreewise. A bounded test case is \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,3,3)\), provided a task-owned exact computation enumerates all Schur columns and positive-degree Pieri relations. Separately, direct source grounding is still needed for the coefficient-ring reduction from ideal minimality to \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\).
